angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 429,247 km at 143.47 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.9701 +/- 0.0174 mas (same row, RUWE 1.04): 143.47 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.617 +/- 0.013 solar radii from Bakos et al. 2015, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HAT-P-54 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015AJ....149..149B/abstract): 429,247 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.645 +/- 0.02 solar masses from Bakos et al. 2015, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HAT-P-54 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015AJ....149..149B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4390 +/- 50 K from Bakos et al. 2015, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HAT-P-54 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015AJ....149..149B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Bakos et al. 2015, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HAT-P-54 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015AJ....149..149B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hat-p-54.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.667, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HAT-P-54 (pscomppars): spectral type K7, from Luo et al. 2018 (http://vizier.u-strasbg.fr/viz-bin/VizieR-3?-source=V/153/stellar4)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, HAT-P-54: main object type *, Star
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HAT-P-54 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.127 dex, from Bakos et al. 2015 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015AJ....149..149B/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HAT-P-54 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.9017, from Bakos et al. 2015 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015AJ....149..149B/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HAT-P-54 (pscomppars): age 3.9 Gyr, from Bakos et al. 2015 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015AJ....149..149B/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: VizieR J/ApJS/264/12/param (Chromospheric activities from LAMOST and K2), column PRot: 14.02 d, the row 0.1 arcsec from the star's J2000 place. The middle of 3 catalogued periods, 2 of them within 20% of it

rotationPeriodsCatalogued.source: VizieR J/A+A/635/A43/table2 (Stellar rotation periods from K2 Campaigns 0-18), column Prot: 15.29 d, the row 0.0 arcsec from the star's J2000 place
VizieR J/ApJS/264/12/param (Chromospheric activities from LAMOST and K2), column PRot: 14.02 d, the row 0.1 arcsec from the star's J2000 place
VizieR J/ApJS/282/29/table5 (Magnetic activity of M-type stars from LAMOST+TESS), column Prot: 8.0193 d, the row 0.0 arcsec from the star's J2000 place

projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HAT-P-54 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 2.35 km/s, from Bakos et al. 2015 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015AJ....149..149B/abstract)
rotationPeriodMeasuredSource: Measured in this project from the K2 mission's own light curve of campaign 0 (packages/telescope-cli/src/archives/tess/reduce.mts), by the method and criteria of Reinhold & Hekker (2020, A&A 635, A43): 14.75 d, the light swinging by 1.1% as the star turns

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
